question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The chairman announced that the company is planning to open three new manufacturing units (a)/ before the end of the financial year, (b)/ as he told the assembled shareholders (c)/ during the annual general meeting. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In reported speech, the present continuous ("is planning") must backshift to the past continuous ("was planning") since the reporting verb "announced" is in the past tense.

◦ Corrected sentence: The chairman announced that the company was planning to open three new manufacturing units before the end of the financial year, as he told the assembled shareholders during the annual general meeting.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "before the end of the financial year," is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "as he told the assembled shareholders" is a proper accompanying clause.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "during the annual general meeting" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• She said that the firm is opening a branch abroad. → the firm was opening a branch abroad (present continuous → past continuous, in backshifting).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The auditor confirmed (a)/ that the company has cleared all its outstanding dues (b)/ before the fiscal year ended. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The present perfect ("has cleared") must backshift to the past perfect ("had cleared") when reported with a past-tense reporting verb such as "confirmed".

◦ Corrected sentence: The auditor confirmed that the company had cleared all its outstanding dues before the fiscal year ended.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The auditor confirmed" correctly introduces the reported statement.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "before the fiscal year ended" is a proper adverbial time clause.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (b).

 

NOTE

 

• He said that the team has finished the survey. → the team had finished the survey (present perfect → past perfect, in backshifting).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

During the review meeting, (a)/ the quality head admitted (b)/ that the testing team overlooked a critical defect (c)/ in the previous production batch. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The simple past ("overlooked") must backshift to the past perfect ("had overlooked") since it reports an action prior to the past-tense reporting verb "admitted".

◦ Corrected sentence: During the review meeting, the quality head admitted that the testing team had overlooked a critical defect in the previous production batch.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "During the review meeting," is a proper introductory phrase.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the quality head admitted" correctly introduces the reported clause.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "in the previous production batch" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• He confessed that he missed the crucial deadline. → he had missed the crucial deadline (simple past → past perfect, in backshifting).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The economist predicted that inflation would ease considerably (a)/ over the subsequent two quarters (b)/ if the central bank tightened its policy, (c)/ a view she said will hold true regardless of global oil prices. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The future "will" must backshift to "would" in the trailing reported clause, since it is governed by the same past-tense reporting verb "said".

◦ Corrected sentence: The economist predicted that inflation would ease considerably over the subsequent two quarters if the central bank tightened its policy, a view she said would hold true regardless of global oil prices.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "would ease" correctly backshifts the future in the main reported clause.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "over the subsequent two quarters" is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "if the central bank tightened its policy," is a properly backshifted conditional clause.

 

NOTE

 

• He argued that the policy will fail regardless of the outcome. → the policy would fail regardless of the outcome (will → would, in backshifting).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

That she can resolve the network issue within twenty-four hours (a)/ once the diagnostic report arrived (b)/ was the assurance the technician gave to the anxious client. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The modal "can" must backshift to "could", since the whole reported clause is governed by the past-tense verb "gave" (the assurance).

◦ Corrected sentence: That she could resolve the network issue within twenty-four hours once the diagnostic report arrived was the assurance the technician gave to the anxious client.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "once the diagnostic report arrived" is a properly backshifted time clause.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "was the assurance the technician gave to the anxious client" correctly completes the sentence.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (a).

 

NOTE

 

• That he can finish the audit by Friday was what he promised. → that he could finish the audit by Friday (can → could, in backshifting).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The weather bureau warned residents (a)/ that flash floods may occur (b)/ in low-lying areas overnight (c)/ following the unusually heavy downpour. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The modal "may" must backshift to "might" since it is reported with the past-tense verb "warned".

◦ Corrected sentence: The weather bureau warned residents that flash floods might occur in low-lying areas overnight following the unusually heavy downpour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The weather bureau warned residents" correctly introduces the reported clause.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "in low-lying areas overnight" is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "following the unusually heavy downpour" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• He said that the bridge may collapse under heavy load. → the bridge might collapse under heavy load (may → might, in backshifting).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The two rival candidates told the election commission (a)/ that they would abide by the model code of conduct (b)/ and that we would refrain from any personal attacks (c)/ during the remaining campaign period. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Since both reported clauses describe the same two candidates, the pronoun must be consistent: "we" is wrongly used instead of "they".

◦ Corrected sentence: The two rival candidates told the election commission that they would abide by the model code of conduct and that they would refrain from any personal attacks during the remaining campaign period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The two rival candidates told the election commission" correctly introduces the reported clauses.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that they would abide by the model code of conduct" correctly uses the shifted pronoun "they".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "during the remaining campaign period" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• The partners said that they would honour the contract and that we would not renegotiate its terms. → that they would not renegotiate its terms (pronoun consistency across coordinated reported clauses).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The delegation informed the press (a)/ that the trade talks scheduled for that week had been postponed indefinitely (b)/ owing to unresolved tariff disagreements. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence correctly shifts the time word "this week" to "that week" and correctly backshifts the passive verb to the past perfect ("had been postponed"), so no correction is required.

◦ Sentence as given: The delegation informed the press that the trade talks scheduled for that week had been postponed indefinitely owing to unresolved tariff disagreements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The delegation informed the press" correctly introduces the reported clause.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that the trade talks scheduled for that week had been postponed indefinitely" is properly backshifted and correctly shifts the time word.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "owing to unresolved tariff disagreements" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• He said that the meeting fixed for this month had been shifted to next month. → fixed for that month had been shifted to the following month (time-word shift, correctly formed).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The curator explained to the visitors that the museum had acquired this rare manuscript (a)/ nearly two centuries before (b)/ from a private European collector (c)/ who had smuggled it out of a war-torn region. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In indirect speech, the demonstrative "this" must shift to "that", since the manuscript is being referred to at a distance from the original moment of speaking.

◦ Corrected sentence: The curator explained to the visitors that the museum had acquired that rare manuscript nearly two centuries before from a private European collector who had smuggled it out of a war-torn region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "nearly two centuries before" is a properly shifted adverbial time phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "from a private European collector" correctly continues the sentence.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "who had smuggled it out of a war-torn region" is a properly formed relative clause.

 

NOTE

 

• She said that she had bought this house long ago. → she had bought that house long ago (this → that, in indirect speech).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The compliance officer asked the vendor (a)/ that whether the invoices matched the delivery challans (b)/ submitted the previous month (c)/ before releasing the final payment. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A yes/no question is reported using only "whether" or "if"; combining it with "that" is ungrammatical, so "that whether" must be simply "whether".

◦ Corrected sentence: The compliance officer asked the vendor whether the invoices matched the delivery challans submitted the previous month before releasing the final payment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The compliance officer asked the vendor" correctly introduces the reported question.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "submitted the previous month" is a proper participial phrase.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before releasing the final payment" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• He asked that whether the goods had been dispatched. → he asked whether the goods had been dispatched ("that whether" is ungrammatical; use "whether" alone).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The scrutiny committee asked the applicant (a)/ whether he had furnished the original mark sheets along with the attested photocopies (b)/ before the deadline expires. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The subordinate time clause verb "expires" must backshift to "expired", since the entire reported passage is governed by a past-tense reporting verb.

◦ Corrected sentence: The scrutiny committee asked the applicant whether he had furnished the original mark sheets along with the attested photocopies before the deadline expired.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The scrutiny committee asked the applicant" correctly introduces the reported question.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "whether he had furnished the original mark sheets along with the attested photocopies" is properly backshifted.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (c).

 

NOTE

 

• She asked whether he had left before the shop closes. → before the shop closed (subordinate clause verb backshifts along with the rest of the sentence).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The board members asked the CEO (a)/ why the quarterly targets had not been met (b)/ despite the additional resources allocated to the sales division, (c)/ and why had the marketing budget been cut simultaneously. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a reported wh-question, the interrogative word order must be replaced by statement word order: "why had the marketing budget" must be "why the marketing budget had".

◦ Corrected sentence: The board members asked the CEO why the quarterly targets had not been met despite the additional resources allocated to the sales division, and why the marketing budget had been cut simultaneously.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The board members asked the CEO" correctly introduces the reported questions.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "why the quarterly targets had not been met" correctly uses statement word order.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "despite the additional resources allocated to the sales division," is a proper concessive phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• He asked why had the shipment been delayed. → why the shipment had been delayed (statement word order restored, no interrogative inversion).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The tourist asked the guide why the museum ___ closed for renovation for several weeks already.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. had been.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The duration marker "for several weeks already" signals the present perfect passive ("has been closed"), which must backshift to the past perfect passive ("had been closed") in a reported wh-question governed by a past-tense reporting verb.

◦ Complete sentence: The tourist asked the guide why the museum had been closed for renovation for several weeks already.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "has been" — the present perfect is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to the past perfect.

 

• Option 3: "was" — the simple past drops the perfect aspect required by the duration marker "for several weeks already".

 

• Option 4: "is being" — the present continuous passive does not correspond to the original tense at all.

 

NOTE

 

• He asked why the office had been shut for repairs for several days already., She asked why the shop had been closed for stocktaking since morning. (duration marker + backshift → past perfect passive).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The counsellor asked the parents (a)/ why their son is missing classes so frequently (b)/ over the past two months. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Since the action has continued over a stated duration ("over the past two months"), the tense must be the past perfect continuous ("had been missing"), not the present continuous "is missing".

◦ Corrected sentence: The counsellor asked the parents why their son had been missing classes so frequently over the past two months.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The counsellor asked the parents" correctly introduces the reported question.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "over the past two months" is a proper duration phrase.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (b).

 

NOTE

 

• He asked why she is feeling unwell for the past few days. → why she had been feeling unwell for the past few days (duration + backshift → past perfect continuous).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The site engineer instructed the labourers (a)/ to wear safety helmets at all times (b)/ while working near the crane and wearing harnesses without fail, (c)/ to prevent any head injuries. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The two coordinated instructions must remain parallel to-infinitives; "wearing harnesses" breaks this parallelism and must be "wear harnesses".

◦ Corrected sentence: The site engineer instructed the labourers to wear safety helmets at all times while working near the crane and wear harnesses without fail, to prevent any head injuries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The site engineer instructed the labourers" correctly introduces the reported instruction.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "to wear safety helmets at all times" correctly uses the to-infinitive.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to prevent any head injuries" is a proper purpose phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• She told the staff to lock the cabinets and switching off the lights before leaving. → and switch off the lights (coordinated instructions must use parallel to-infinitives).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The lifeguard warned the children ___ near the deep end of the pool without adult supervision.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. not to go.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A negative imperative is reported using the reporting verb followed by the object and "not to" + base verb, with "not" placed before "to".

◦ Complete sentence: The lifeguard warned the children not to go near the deep end of the pool without adult supervision.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "to not go" — the negation is misplaced; the standard form places "not" before "to": "not to go".

 

• Option 2: "not going" — the gerund is wrongly used instead of the required infinitive "not to go".

 

• Option 3: "don't go" — the original imperative form is wrongly retained instead of being converted into the infinitive form.

 

NOTE

 

• The guard told them, "Don't cross the yellow line." → the guard warned them not to cross the yellow line (negative imperative → warned/told + object + not to + base verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The safety officer ordered the workers evacuating the building immediately (a)/ upon hearing the fire alarm (b)/ during the unannounced drill. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An order is reported using "ordered" followed by the object and the to-infinitive; the gerund "evacuating" must be "to evacuate".

◦ Corrected sentence: The safety officer ordered the workers to evacuate the building immediately upon hearing the fire alarm during the unannounced drill.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "upon hearing the fire alarm" is a proper participial phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "during the unannounced drill" correctly completes the sentence.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (a).

 

NOTE

 

• The captain ordered the sailors lowering the sails at once. → ordered the sailors to lower the sails (ordered + object + to-infinitive, not a gerund).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The spectators exclaimed (a)/ that what a thrilling final over it had been (b)/ as the winning six sailed over the boundary (c)/ on the very last ball of the match. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An exclamatory sentence is reported as a plain statement; the exclamatory structure "what a...!" must be dropped, so "that what a thrilling final over it had been" must be "that it had been a thrilling final over".

◦ Corrected sentence: The spectators exclaimed that it had been a thrilling final over as the winning six sailed over the boundary on the very last ball of the match.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The spectators exclaimed" correctly introduces the exclamatory report.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "as the winning six sailed over the boundary" is a proper accompanying clause.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "on the very last ball of the match" correctly completes the sentence.

 

NOTE

 

• He exclaimed that what a wonderful surprise this was. → he exclaimed that it was a wonderful surprise (exclamatory structure dropped, converted into a plain statement).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

She exclaimed that what a terrible mistake she had made during the annual budget presentation.
option_1: exclaimed with regret what a terrible mistake she had made
option_2: exclaimed that she has made a terrible mistake
option_3: exclaimed with regret that she had made a terrible mistake
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. exclaimed with regret that she had made a terrible mistake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An exclamation of regret is reported using a phrase such as "exclaimed with regret that", dropping the exclamatory "what a...!" structure and converting it into a plain statement.

◦ Corrected sentence: She exclaimed with regret that she had made a terrible mistake during the annual budget presentation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "exclaimed with regret what a terrible mistake..." — the exclamatory structure "what a" is wrongly retained inside the noun clause.

 

• Option 2: "exclaimed that she has made..." — "has made" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "had made".

 

• Option 4: "No improvement required" — incorrect, since the exclamatory structure in the original must be converted into a plain statement.

 

NOTE

 

• He exclaimed that what a foolish decision he had taken. → he exclaimed with regret that he had taken a foolish decision ("what a...!" of regret → "exclaimed with regret that").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The residents' association proposed that they should install additional security cameras (a)/ at every entrance of the housing complex (b)/ before the onset of the festive season, (c)/ and requested that let the maintenance team survey the site first. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A reported clause cannot retain the imperative form "let"; "requested that let the maintenance team survey" must be "requested that the maintenance team should survey".

◦ Corrected sentence: The residents' association proposed that they should install additional security cameras at every entrance of the housing complex before the onset of the festive season, and requested that the maintenance team should survey the site first.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "proposed that they should install" is a properly formed suggestion.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "at every entrance of the housing complex" is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "before the onset of the festive season," correctly completes the first clause.

 

NOTE

 

• They suggested that let the committee review the budget again. → they suggested that the committee should review the budget again ("let" cannot appear inside a reported clause).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The event committee suggested that let them shift the venue indoors (a)/ in view of the unpredictable weather forecast (b)/ issued by the meteorological department. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A suggestion reported with "suggested that" must use "...should...", not the imperative form "let them"; "suggested that let them shift" must be "suggested that they should shift".

◦ Corrected sentence: The event committee suggested that they should shift the venue indoors in view of the unpredictable weather forecast issued by the meteorological department.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "in view of the unpredictable weather forecast" is a proper reason phrase.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "issued by the meteorological department" correctly completes the sentence.

 

• Option (d) No error — this is incorrect since an error exists in part (a).

 

NOTE

 

• He proposed that let the two teams merge their resources. → he proposed that the two teams should merge their resources ("suggested/proposed that...should", not "let").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The investigators found (a)/ that the fire alarm had malfunctioned several hours before the blaze had actually started (b)/ on the factory's ground floor, (c)/ delaying the evacuation process significantly. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Of the two past actions joined by "before", the earlier one ("malfunctioned") correctly takes the past perfect, but the later one must remain in the simple past: "had actually started" must be "actually started".

◦ Corrected sentence: The investigators found that the fire alarm had malfunctioned several hours before the blaze actually started on the factory's ground floor, delaying the evacuation process significantly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The investigators found" correctly introduces the reported clause.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "on the factory's ground floor," correctly continues the sentence.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "delaying the evacuation process significantly" is a proper participial phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• She said that she had left the office before the storm had hit the city. → before the storm hit the city (the later of two past actions stays in the simple past).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The twins told their teacher that ___ had completed the science project together over the weekend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. they.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Since the twins themselves are the speakers being reported in the third person, the pronoun must be "they".

◦ Complete sentence: The twins told their teacher that they had completed the science project together over the weekend.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "we" — this would only be correct if the twins were being quoted directly, not reported in the third person.

 

• Option 2: "he" — the wrong number is used; the twins are plural, so "he" (singular) is incorrect.

 

• Option 4: "I" — the wrong person is used entirely; the sentence is a third-person report, not a first-person quotation.

 

NOTE

 

• The partners said that ___ had signed the agreement. → they had signed the agreement (third-person plural subject reported as "they").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The visa officer asked the applicant ___ he had visited any conflict-affected country in the past five years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. whether.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A yes/no question is reported using the connector "whether" (or "if"), not "that" or a wh-word such as "what"/"which".

◦ Complete sentence: The visa officer asked the applicant whether he had visited any conflict-affected country in the past five years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "that" — "that" is the wrong connector for a yes/no question.

 

• Option 2: "what" — "what" is a wh-word and is not appropriate for reporting a yes/no question.

 

• Option 3: "which" — "which" is also a wh-word and is inappropriate here.

 

NOTE

 

• He asked her ___ she had renewed her passport. → whether she had renewed her passport (yes/no question → whether/if).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

My uncle told me last month that he will visit us again next winter once his health improved.
option_1: that he would visit us again the following winter
option_2: that he will visit us again the following winter
option_3: that he would visit them again next winter
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. that he would visit us again the following winter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The future "will" must backshift to "would", and the time word "next winter" must shift to "the following winter"; the pronoun "us" correctly stays unchanged since the reporter is included among the people visited.

◦ Corrected sentence: My uncle told me last month that he would visit us again the following winter once his health improved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "that he will visit us again the following winter" — "will" is wrongly left unchanged instead of backshifting to "would".

 

• Option 3: "that he would visit them again next winter" — "us" is wrongly changed to "them"; since the reporter ("me") is part of "us", the pronoun should stay "us", and "next winter" is also wrongly left unchanged.

 

• Option 4: "No improvement required" — incorrect, since both "will" and "next winter" need to change.

 

NOTE

 

• She said that she will call us again next Monday. → she would call us again the following Monday (will → would; time-word shift; inclusive pronoun retained).
